children.text: Tapping ANYWHERE on the 7″ readout opens this volume overlay (#698) — the whole glass is the touch target; there is no dedicated button. It is drawn as a full-screen panel on $bg-stage, not a modal over dimmed content: at 7″ a modal frame wastes pixels, and the panel keeps the 2 m type discipline. The overlay is a SINGLE full-width SCROLLING list (ListView): the header (INPUTS caption + BACK TO STAGE chip) is PINNED at the top and the list scrolls under it; rows stay full-width (1854) at 110 high so sliders remain touch-controllable — no column compression. The drawing shows the honest viewport: the rows that fit, the next row (TRACK 6) cut by the bottom edge, and a slim scrollbar hint on the right — TRACK 7–8 exist below the fold. Dismissal: tap the BACK TO STAGE chip, tap any dead space, or 8 s of inactivity auto-reverts to the readout. Both groups are DYNAMIC: INPUTS shows one row per configured input (two drawn), TRACKS shows the LIVE TRACK COUNT — the engine runs 8; only 4 carry custom names, and default-named tracks (TRACK 5–8, l10n defaultTrackName) render their name in $text-secondary, the tone the tracks screen uses for a track's default identity, while custom names are $text-primary. Each row is the ParamSlider idiom (ThalA) scaled to finger + 2 m size: name 42/700 in a 300 column, $bg-surface capsule track with $accent-surface fill and 4 px $accent right-edge marker, value 40 Inter (signed dB, one decimal, true minus — signal_style.dart format; tabular numerals at implementation), and a CONFIG ZONE at the row's right edge: an 88×110 chevron target. Interaction contract: tap/drag anywhere on the row = volume; tap the chevron zone = that element's own full-screen config panel (STAGE / readout-volumes-input, STAGE / readout-volumes-track); the panel's BACK chip returns to this list; the 8 s auto-revert chain applies from the panels too (panel → list → readout). Wire protocol: volume and config commands flow sub→main over the window channel — the first control path in that direction (the readout was previously display-only).
